name: Genome assembly from long reads (Flye and QUAST)
description: Put long Nanopore or PacBio reads of a microbial genome together without a reference, then measure how good the assembly is.
details: Use this to assemble the genome of a cultured organism, such as a bacterium or a plasmid, from long reads. Flye builds the assembly, polishes it once, and also writes a table that says which contigs are circular and how deeply each is covered. QUAST then reports how many contigs there are, how long they are (N50) and the total size; with a reference genome of a close relative it also measures how much of it is covered and how many misassemblies there are. The setup step asks what kind of long reads you have (it starts at Nanopore, older chemistry or unknown) and, optionally, the rough genome size (for example 5m for a bacterium). For a good assembly you need about 30 times coverage or more, and reads that are mostly longer than a few thousand bases; filter poor reads first (the template "Nanopore reads from FASTQ to coverage" shows how, with chopper) if your data is mixed. For short reads use "Genome assembly from short reads (SPAdes and QUAST)".

inputs.label: Long reads
inputs.hint: One FASTQ or FASTA file of long reads, plain or compressed.

inputs.label: Reference genome (optional)
inputs.hint: A genome of the same or a close species as FASTA. QUAST compares the assembly with it. Leave empty to judge the assembly on its own.

settings.label: Kind of reads
settings.hint: Tells Flye how many errors to expect. Pick the newest Nanopore chemistry for reads basecalled at Q20 or better.

settings.label: Expected genome size (optional)
settings.hint: For example 5m for a 5 million base bacterium, or 25k. Leave empty to let Flye work it out.

outputs.label: Contig table
outputs.hint: Length, depth and whether each contig is circular.

outputs.label: Assembly graph
outputs.hint: GFA file; open it in Bandage to see how the contigs connect.

outputs.label: Quality summary
outputs.hint: Text with the number of contigs, N50 and total length.

outputs.label: Quality table
outputs.hint: The same numbers as a table.

references.label: Kolmogorov M, Yuan J, Lin Y, Pevzner PA. Assembly of long, error-prone reads using repeat graphs. Nature Biotechnology 2019;37:540-546.
Gurevich A, Saveliev V, Vyahhi N, Tesler G. QUAST: quality assessment tool for genome assemblies. Bioinformatics 2013;29:1072-1075.
